finding: Ordered retained pages and rate-limit headers do not by themselves prove exhaustive pagination. GitHub documents the response Link header, specifically rel=next, as the authoritative continuation mechanism; a complete retained traversal must therefore preserve and reconcile each next target with the following request URL and terminate only when rel=next is absent.
design_implication: Require a valid pagination-link-chain proof for both exhaustive clients before reconciliation evidence can be promoted. Keep rate-limit proof, provider-ceiling checks, response-body digests, exact-commit binding, and secondary-limit handling as independent fail-closed gates.
uncertainty: Internal Link-chain consistency does not authenticate retained records by itself.
Endpoints may omit calculable last links; the contract intentionally relies only on rel=next continuity and terminal absence.
Secondary rate-limit status cannot be proven absent through primary rate-limit headers.
falsification_route: Run deterministic Node tests and reject any failing case.
Execute both authenticated exhaustive clients for one exact commit and retain request URLs plus raw Link headers.
Reject any non-terminal page without rel=next, any mismatch between rel=next and the following request URL, or any terminal page that still advertises rel=next.
Compare against an independently retained traversal and preserve disagreement as fail-closed.

queue_effect.next_action: Integrate buildPaginationLinkChainProof into the retained-evidence CLI for both clients, run its tests, then execute authenticated exact-commit traversals and retain raw Link headers with the existing response and digest evidence.

specialist_registry_change: none; no durable capability gap established
